subject: Dedicated capacity recap: Lumos Health - reserved GPUs & SLA
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Hart <j.hart@lumoshealth.com>, Priya Mehta <p.mehta@lumoshealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, May 18, 2027 at 3:12 PM PDT
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps  Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs, isolation, SLA)

Hi Jordan / Priya

Thanks again for the time today. Wanted to capture the key points and next steps so we're all aligned. Happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Call summary (high level):
- Primary pain: production latency spikes during daily batch runs and unpredictable tail latency causing degraded UX for clinicians.
- Current infra: in-house inference on mixed GPU fleet with noisy neighbors; caching/kv is limited.
- Goal: move critical inference / patient triage models to a dedicated footprint to guarantee latency, isolation, and predictable cost.

Dedicated capacity requirements we discussed:
- Reserved pool: initial target = 8x A100-class GPUs (to support concurrent low-latency requests and nightly batch throughput).
- Isolation: VPC + private networking; model weights and inference logs must remain isolated from multi-tenant tenants.
- Scaling plan: autoscale policy to allow short-term burst to +25% capacity for scheduled batch windows; target steady-state scale to support 10% month-over-month growth.
- SLA targets: uptime SLA 99.95% (monthly), p95 inference latency target <= 150ms for interactive flows; preferrable fallbacks to smaller quantized model on overload.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence and KMS integration are required for production; procurement will need our SOC2 report and data processing addendum.

Next steps / asks:
1) I'll send a draft proposal and pricing estimate that maps reserved GPU commit to monthly cost and overage behavior.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Vivek to finalize network/VPC details and the autoscaling pattern (can we do this Thurs or Fri?).
3) Procurement: Priya / procurement@lumoshealth once you confirm required contract terms we'll route to Legal / Contracts for SOW and DPA.

Tentative timeline: pilot on dedicated capacity targeted to start ~June 7 (dependent on contracting).

If that aligns, I'll circulate the proposal + a short SOW and a technical appendix for review.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: none in this email (proposal to follow)

Thanks Marissa this looks right to me. A couple quick clarifications: 
- The 8x A100 estimate is consistent with what our infra team guessed during the call, but can you include a short note on expected throughput (qps) and batch window sizing that motivated the 8 GPUs?
- Procurement question: do you have a standard reserved-capacity contract length (12 vs 36 months) and discounts for annual commit? We'll need a pricing tier we can show Finance.

Procurement is copied  Priya, if there are any non-negotiable terms on your side please flag.

Also, June 7 pilot start would be ideal; if we can get a proposal + SOW this week we'll prioritize the approval flow.

Timeline: if we can get both docs by EOD Thu (May 20), I'll bundle into a proposal and send to Lumos + procurement.

Marissa

Subject: Proposal & SOW (draft)  Reserved capacity for Lumos Health (RDW-2389)

Hi Jordan / Priya

Attached are the proposal and a light technical appendix for the reserved-capacity setup: RDW_Proposal_Lumos_Reserved_Capacity_v1.pdf and Lumos-MAP.xlsx (monthly autoscaling plan).

High-level summary:
- Reserved commit: 8x A100-class GPUs (reserved pool)  recommended starting utilization profile assumes 65-75% steady-state utilization outside batch windows.
- Isolation: Dedicated VPC + private peering; model artifacts stored in customer-scoped S3 buckets with KMS encryption.
- Autoscaling: allow +25% short-term burst for nightly batch windows; burst capacity subject to booked spare capacity and pre-agreed fallback policy.
- SLA: 99.95% monthly uptime; p95 interactive latency <= 150ms for provisioned traffic. Overage and degraded-mode behavior documented in the appendix.
- Pricing: included in attached proposal (12-month and 36-month options, with discounted annual price for 36-month commit).

Next suggested steps:
1) Please review the attached proposal and the technical appendix.
2) If the SOW looks good, confirm procurement contact and preferred contract length so I can route to Legal for a DPA and SOW signature.
3) Schedule the technical deep-dive with Vivek this Friday (May 21) at 11:00 AM PDT  is that time okay?

I've added a DocuSign link for the initial non-binding proposal acceptance (link below) we typically move to a full SOW once procurement confirms terms.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/companies/67890

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the proposal.

Best,
Marissa
